newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia to extend gas selloff deadline - report.
newsitem.headline: Latvia to extend gas selloff deadline - report.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) board is expected on Thursday again to postpone the deadline for Germany's Preussen and Ruhrgas to buy a stake in Latvian Gas, Janis Naglis, LPA manager told Diena newspaper.
"The new deadline will be set for April 1, if not later," Naglis told the newspaper.
Strategic investors Preussen and Ruhrgas and Russia's Gazprom were due to decide on Latvian Gas by February 16.
Latvia is ready to improve the gas company's debt situation and needs time to write-off and capitalise its debts, Naglis was quoted by the newspaper as saying.
Some 17.3 million lats of local council's debt are expected to be written-off while eight million lats of Latvian Gas debt to the state budget will be capitalised.
"A government decision is required on these issues and therefore we will extend the deadline," Naglis told Diena.
Preussen and Ruhrgas formed a consortium to buy a stake in Latvian Gas while Gazprom was taking part as a separate partner.
The German companies have delayed signing up for the Latvian Gas shares due to the company's high debts.
